Get or set the manimR configuration

Source: R/config.R
manim_config.Rd

Called with no arguments, returns the current configuration as a list. Named arguments update it; an unknown name is an error, as upstream's config. The config object gives the same settings with upstream's config$name syntax, with_manim_config() and tempconfig() change them for a block of code, and digest_config_file() reads them from a manim.cfg file.

Usage

manim_config(...)

Arguments

...

Named settings.

Value

The configuration list (including the derived frame_width, frame_x_radius, frame_y_radius, transparent and save_last_frame), invisibly when setting.

Details

The settings, with upstream's names and defaults:

  • Frame: quality (a flag "l" 854x480 at 15 fps, "m" 1280x720 at 30, "h" 1920x1080 at 60, "p" 2560x1440 at 60, "k" 3840x2160 at 60, or a preset name of QUALITIES), pixel_width, pixel_height, frame_size (both at once), frame_rate, frame_height (8), frame_width (derived from the aspect ratio unless set), frame_x_radius, frame_y_radius, background_color, background_opacity, transparent (TRUE sets background_opacity to 0).

  • Output: format, the artifact a render writes: "auto" (the default: MP4, or MOV when transparent; a scene without animations is saved as its last frame), "mp4", "mov", "webm", "gif", "png" (only the last frame), "png-sequence" (every frame) or "none". save_last_frame = TRUE is short for format = "png". dry_run renders without writing files, save_sections also writes one video per section, zero_pad (4) is the number of digits in PNG sequence file names, output_file names the artifact (relative to its directory below), from_animation_number and upto_animation_number (-1: all) select animations.

  • Directories, with {name} placeholders resolved by get_dir(): media_dir (a folder media in the session's temporary directory; set it, for example to "media", to keep the output; manim_cli() uses "media" in the working directory, as upstream), video_dir ("{media_dir}/videos/{module_name}/{quality}"), images_dir, sections_dir, partial_movie_dir, tex_dir, text_dir, log_dir, assets_dir (where sounds and images are looked up), input_file (the script being rendered; its name is the module name) and manimR's module_name for scenes rendered from R code ("manimR").

  • Encoding: video_codec, pixel_format (both "auto") and video_encoder_options (a named list of ffmpeg options such as list(crf = "18")) for the cached video segments; max_inflight_encoders and encoder_queue_size are validated but encoding runs in the R process, one segment at a time.

  • Caching: disable_caching, disable_caching_warning, max_files_cached (100; -1 keeps all), and manimR's flush_cache.

  • Presentation and logging: preview (open the result), preview_command, show_in_file_browser, verbosity ("INFO"), progress_bar, log_to_file (write a log per scene to log_dir), media_loglevel.

  • LaTeX: tex_template (a TexTemplate()), tex_template_file, no_latex_cleanup (keep .aux, .dvi and .log files in tex_dir).

  • Other: seed (random seed of every scene), renderer ("cairo"; "opengl" is accepted and renders with the Cairo style renderer, the only one ported), plugins, write_all, scene_names, notify_outdated_version, and the OpenGL window settings enable_gui, live_preview, gui_location, fullscreen, window_position, window_size, window_monitor, use_projection_fill_shaders, use_projection_stroke_shaders, enable_wireframe, which have no effect on the Cairo style renderer (asking for a live preview is an error, as upstream), and the Jupyter settings media_embed and media_width.

  • manimR only: ffmpeg and typst (paths of those programs) and curve_tolerance.

Examples

old <- manim_config(quality = "l")
manim_config()$pixel_width
#> [1] 854
manim_config(quality = old$quality)
